artworks.title: Imaginary View of S. Giacomo di Rialto [upper right]
artworks.description: The image features an urban square with a large building that has a clock on its facade, flanked by arches. The sky takes up much of the top area. The scene includes columns with Corinthian capitals, an open area with small human figures, and various architectural details. The etching shows fine, linear brushstrokes creating detailed textures. The color scheme is monochromatic in black and white, emphasizing lines and shadows. In the background, there are buildings and ships, implying a waterway or harbor.

artworks.title: The Terrace [lower right]
artworks.description: The image shows an urban scene with buildings, rooftops, and architectural details as seen from an elevated position. The style is characterized by detailed linework and cross-hatching to depict textures. The scene includes figures, plants, and various architectural elements. The sky is lightly sketched in the background.

artworks.title: The Market at Dolo [lower left]
artworks.description: The image shows a riverside scene with various figures engaged in activities. Closest to us, individuals tend to baskets and market stalls. Tents and goods suggest a marketplace setting. In the background is a large, ornate building reflected in the river. Beyond the river, there is a mountainous landscape. The sky features textured clouds in fine linework. The monochrome color palette adds a classic tone to the scene. The detailed technique captures both architecture and human activity, creating a lively historical scene.

artworks.title: Landscape with the Pilgrim at Prayer [upper left]
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape viewed from a slightly elevated perspective. The horizon is high in the composition, partially obscured by a large hill. Atop the hill are structures, including a gateway and various buildings. The drawing uses fine lines for texture and depth. The color palette is monochromatic, with shades of gray and black emphasizing line work and shadow. In the foreground, a figure leans on a stick, and another person sits in a small boat on the right. A path leads up the hill, with a shelter visible on the left, against the sky marked with horizontal strokes.

artworks.title: The Equestrian Monument [upper right]
artworks.description: The image depicts architectural structures, a statue of a horse and rider on a pedestal, figures, animals, ruins, a bridge-like structure, towers, and the sky. The point of view is from a slightly lowered angle, with the horizon towards the upper third of the image. The artwork is detailed, using fine line work and a monochrome color palette of black and white.

artworks.title: Mountain Landscape with Five Bridges [lower right]
artworks.description: The image displays a landscape with a slightly elevated point of view. In the distance, there are rolling hills, scattered trees, and a horizon line meeting the sky. Central to the scene are distant structures, potentially buildings or a castle. The artwork showcases detailed etchings with thin lines, capturing specifics like tree foliage and water streams. The image is monochromatic, using various shades of black and white for contrast and texture. Closest to the viewer is a bridge over a waterway, with a coach and travelers moving along the path. Further beyond are trees, structures, and a textured sky.

artworks.title: Landscape with a Woman at a Well [lower left]
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape scene created in a detailed etching style. The scene includes a path leading past a group of figures near a large stone building with wooden elements. There is a stream or canal with wooden crossings. In the distance, church domes and hills are visible under a sky filled with cross-hatching brushstrokes. The color palette is black and white, emphasizing shadow and highlights.

artworks.title: Landscape with Tower and Two Ruined Pillars [left]
artworks.description: The image is an etching of a landscape with a strong horizontal expanse. The horizon is in the middle, with a tower and surrounding structures in the distance. A woman on a path with an object and a dog is in the foreground. People further up the path interact with the environment. To the left are rooftops and a spire, and to the right, natural elements and architectural ruins. Sparse, linear cloud formations fill the sky. The etching uses a black and white palette with detailed, crosshatched strokes for depth and texture.

artworks.title: Landscape with Ruined Monuments [right]
artworks.description: The image features architectural elements, including a large stone pillar and an ornate archway, set against a background that includes trees, a pyramid-like structure, and buildings with spires. The artwork is characterized by detailed etchings with fine lines and hatching techniques to show depth and texture. The color palette is monochromatic, in shades of black and white.

artworks.title: The Little Monument [left]
artworks.description: The image shows a view near a body of water, with a cityscape in the distance. The horizon is near the observer's eye level, with architectural silhouettes visible on it. On the right, there is a column-like monument in the water, and a person rowing a boat on the left. A tree's branches frame the top right of the scene. Fine lines create texture in the water and branches. The artwork has a monochromatic palette dominated by black ink on a light background.

artworks.title: The Bishop's Tomb [center]
artworks.description: The image depicts an architectural scene with classical elements. A tree trunk with foliage is on the left, contrasting with the structured elements around it. Columns, a statue, and architectural details are prominent. An archway and columns create depth on the right. In the background, there are hills or mountains with a small building. The artwork features detailed linework, cross-hatching, and a monochromatic color palette emphasizing black and white tones.

artworks.title: The Wagon Passing over a Bridge
artworks.description: The image depicts an etching featuring a view from a low angle of a curved stone bridge. The horizon is positioned along the top third of the image, with the bridge and a distant structure visible on it. Close to us are figures sitting by the water's edge beneath the bridge. A cart pulled by oxen and led by figures traverses the bridge. Above, a rustic-style building sits to the left of the bridge, with its roof edge paralleling the bridge's arc. The technique involves precise, parallel horizontal lines filling the background and detailed, slightly wavering lines defining the main elements like the bridge and building. The color palette consists of black lines and the white of the paper, creating strong contrast to emphasize the intricate detailing of the etching.

artworks.title: American Winter Scenes: Morning
artworks.medium: lithograph with hand coloring on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: This print depicts a winter scene from a slightly elevated perspective. The view captures a group of people engaging in various activities on a frozen river surrounded by snow-covered hills and trees, some bare and some with green needles. In the distance, a wooden bridge spans the frozen water, and distant houses, trees, and birds are seen against gentle snowy hills under soft sunlight. At the bottom of the painting, some people sled down a hill onto the frozen water while others skate on the ice. The people wear warm buttoned coats in shades of yellow, green, brown, and blue. Some wear brown hats and red scarves. In the bottom right corner, large chunks have been taken out of the ice, and thin cracks form. The painting has a color palette of blues and whites, contrasting with warm tones from the clothing of the people. The cloudy sky above is mostly gray with some patches of pale blue peeking through. At the bottom a line of text reads "AMERICAN WINTER SCENES."

artworks.title: Peytona and Fashion: In Their Great Match for $20,000. Over the Union Course L.I. May 13th. 1845, Won by Peytona. Time 7:39 3/4, 7:45 1/4
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: This is a painting of a historic horse race event. The image captures a horse race between two horses, identified as Peytona and Fashion, in front of a cheering crowd. The action happens at the forefront, where two horses race along a dirt track. The riders on the horses are focused on the race, each dressed colorfully. The crowd lines the track, with many spectators looking on excitedly. In the background, various buildings and a carriage add to the scene. The painting likely commemorates a race held on May 13, 1845, as noted in the scripted details at the bottom of the image. This is in the style of 19th-century American lithography, capturing events in vibrant scenes.

artworks.title: Across the Continent: "Westward the Course of Empire Takes Its Way"
artworks.medium: lithograph with hand coloring and touches of gum arabic on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: Train tracks slice across a flat, grassy landscape with log cabins to our left and a river and mountains to our right in this horizontal lithograph. The scene is printed with vivid colors and is packed with tiny details. A train engine puffing black smoke pulls five cars from the bottom right corner away into the distance, angling to our left before disappearing on the horizon, which comes about three quarters of the way up the composition. Writing across the tops of the first three cars reads, “Through line New York San Francisco” in all caps. The open windows on the fourth car are crowded with riders. Tucked into the lower left corner, eleven log-built structures are mostly clustered closely together. Children play and run around the open door of the building closest to us, which is labeled “Public School.” Other people in long skirts or suits, some in hats, stand waving near the tracks. Four men in long-sleeved shirts or jackets and long pants, all with hats, chop down trees or hold shovels in a wooded area in the lower left corner. Four wagons, three of them covered and drawn by ox, move away from the town. All of the people in the town and on the train appear to have pale, peachy skin. The black smoke pouring from the train engine turns to slate gray where it blankets the ground to our right. Two people with brown skin, long black hair, feathered headdresses, and yellow and red clothing sit on horseback and are nearly swallowed by the smoke. A glassy, blue river winds into the distance to our left. One person is in a canoe on the river, which is lined by pines and other trees. White clouds kick up against the snowy mountain peaks that span the right half of the horizon against an otherwise bright blue sky. The margin around the scene is foxed, speckled brown against the white paper. Printed below the image, in all caps, the title reads, “Across the Continent. “Westward the Course of Empire Takes Its Way.” In tiny letters, immediately below the printed image are three more inscriptions. They read, to the left, “J.M. Ives, Del.” At the center, “Entered according to Act of Congress in the year AD. 1868 by Currier & Ives in the Clerks Office of the District Court of the United States for the Southern District of New York.” And to the right, in all caps, “Drawn by F.F. Palmer.”

artworks.title: Broadway, New York: From the Western Union Telegraph Building Looking North
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon

artworks.title: The Farm-Yard in Winter
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph, with touches of gum arabic, on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: This print depicts a winter farm scene. On the left is a large gray barn, its roof covered in snow and some small black birds. The large doors of the barn are open to reveal piles of yellow hay and a horse in a stall, with two men in dark jackets and hats standing on either side of the stall. In front of the barn's doors, cows, ducks, and chickens stand in a snowy yard bordered by a wooden fence, another pile of hay on the left. On the right are more snow-covered buildings, leafless trees, and distant gray hills under a pale gray sky with white clouds. Below the print are two lines of text.

artworks.title: Home to Thanksgiving
artworks.artist: John Schutler after George Henry Durrie
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: In muted blue, yellow, gray, and white against cream-colored paper, this horizontal print shows animals and pale-skinned people gathered around and among a snow-covered house and barn. To our right, the two-story farmhouse is constructed with horizontal, parchment-brown planks, and the structure is cropped by the right edge of the composition. Two women, two men, and a child gather near the darkened, open door of the farmhouse, which is protected by an overhanging roof. One woman standing in the doorway wears a long, cobalt-blue dress with a white apron and bonnet. On her hip, she holds a small child wearing a black garment and a white bonnet. Two men and the other woman stand near the door, and the two men shake hands. At the center of this trio, an older, cleanshaven man with white hair faces us as he shakes hands with a younger man with a goatee, to our left. The younger man and the woman stand with their backs to us, their bodies angled toward the older man. The men wear long black coats, black pants, and dark hats while the woman here wears a long, cranberry-red dress under a black coat and black hat. The adults all smile faintly. A charcoal-gray horse stands alongside the porch to our left, wearing a ring of sleigh bells like a belt. The horse is hitched to a blue sleigh on runners, which has a brown blanket inside. Closer to us, at the center of the composition, two steers, one brown and one black, stand attached to a sled loaded with gray logs. A man stands alongside the logs, looking back toward the farmhouse with his body angled to our right. He wears a blue coat, brown pants, and a gray hat, and holds a tall, thin staff or branch upright with his right hand. On the ground close to us, gray footprints and blue ice spread out in the otherwise pristine snow, and a small black dog walks toward the steers, to our left. Along the left half of the composition and farther back, the barn walls are clad in vertical, oatmeal-brown planks. An open shed is cut off by the left edge of the composition, and it holds what could be a ladder and carriage. Beyond it, there is a fenced in area in front of the barn with two cows, almost a dozen chickens, and a rooster standing in the snow. One door to the barn is open, and hay is piled high inside. A man with his back to us holds a long stick, presumably moving the hay. Two tall, dark gray, bare tree trunks grow in the fenced-in area to our left, and more grow up behind the house to our right. Another pile of hay, taller than the lean-to next to it, is dusted with snow. A snow-covered field beyond the buildings leads back to misty, gray-blue mountains. The hazy sky above has a pale, butter-yellow glow to our right against the ice-blue sky. The print is signed in the lower corners, with “G.H. Durrie 186” to our left and “Jno Schuller Del.” to our right. The work has text printed in the margin beneath the image. The largest text, at the bottom center, reads, “HOME TO THANKSGIVING.” Smaller text above it, immediately under the image, reads, “Entered according to Act of Congress AD 1867 by Currier & Ives in the Clerks Office of the District Court of the United States for the Southern District of N.Y.” Under the main title, it reads, “NEW YORK PUBLISHED BY CURRIER & IVES, 152 NASSAU STREET.”

artworks.title: Summer Scenes in New York Harbor
artworks.artist: after Charles Parsons and Lyman W. Atwater
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: The image shows a panoramic view of New York Harbor from an overhead perspective. The horizon is in the upper third of the image, revealing several ships along the harbor. The artwork is a detailed lithograph depicting ships with sails, flags, and rigging. The color palette includes soft blues for the water and sky, and hints of cream, brown, red, and blue in the sails, flags, and rowers' shirts. In the foreground, rowers in red and blue shirts are seen paddling in long boats. Further back are larger sailing ships and steamships with multiple masts adorned with flags. The background displays a soft sky with scattered clouds.

artworks.title: The Bostonian's Paying the Excise-Man, or Tarring & Feathering
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 35.1 x 25.4 cm (13 13/16 x 10 in.)
artworks.description: The image shows a group of men holding down another person. The central figure is laid out and covered with feathers. His facial expression appears distressed, with long hair. The other individuals wear long coats, hats, and trousers. One man is pouring liquid labeled "Tea" on the central figure. In the background, there are ships and a large tree labeled "LIBERTY TREE" with a sign attached. The scene is monochrome, with shades of brown and tan.

artworks.title: Horse
artworks.medium: chalk and pastel counterproof on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a horse. It shows the side profile of a horse in earthy tones on a light background. The horse is standing in a natural pose, with its body and head outlined with confident strokes. The use of pastel colors gives the horse a sense of texture and volume, capturing light and shadow play on its muscular structure. The drawing's simplicity and skilled suggestion of form and proportion suggest a study focused on capturing the horse's serene elegance and natural beauty.

artworks.title: Three Studies of Ludovic Halévy Standing
artworks.medium: charcoal counterproof on buff wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: This drawing shows three identical men in profile, facing the left, wearing high top hats and long coats. They are all leaning forward slightly with their hands in their pockets. The sketch is done in a loose drawing style, with little detail visible in the men’s faces. The background is plain, off-white paper.

artworks.title: Woman by a Fireplace
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: The image depicts a dimly lit interior scene. A three-armed candelabrum to the left casts a faint glow, illuminating the surroundings with heavy shadows. In the center, vague shapes and outlines suggest the presence of draped figures or objects merging into the dark ambiance. The atmosphere is moody and mysterious, with a play of light and shadow adding drama to the scene.

artworks.title: Boxeurs (The Boxers)
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon
artworks.description: The image shows two men in a fighting stance in a side view. Both men are positioned with their fists up, leaning slightly backward. On the left is a shirtless man with dark skin, short hair, and light-colored trousers. On the right is a shirtless man with light skin, dark hair, and striped trousers. A crowd surrounds the fighters, some seated and some standing. The background is a shaded sketch of outdoor terrain under a cloudy sky. An object resembling a jug is next to them.
